krieg.gelaende.ebene: Plain: good for armour, open to air strikes
krieg.gelaende.berge: Mountains: tough for any offensive, mountain war is costly
krieg.gelaende.stadt: City: street fighting, slow and costly
krieg.gelaende.insel: Island: cannot be taken without a navy
krieg.gelaende.kueste: Coast: army and navy complement each other
krieg.ressource.korridor: land corridor; the route is under US development rights (TRIPP, 49 + 50 years), the peace treaty is only initialled
krieg.einsatz.luft.name: Air and drone campaign
krieg.einsatz.luft.text: Few own losses and heavy pressure on the enemy and his infrastructure, but air strikes alone only take border areas. Suited to forcing negotiations.
krieg.einsatz.boden.name: Ground offensive
krieg.einsatz.boden.text: The only way to take ground deep inside the country. Fast on plains, slow in mountains and cities; heavy losses, the home front tires faster.
krieg.einsatz.see.name: Naval blockade
krieg.einsatz.see.text: Closes ports and sea lanes: islands fall and the enemy grows poorer faster. Also hurts your own trade; useless inland.
krieg.einsatz.stellvertreter.name: Local allied forces
krieg.einsatz.stellvertreter.text: Allied groups fight with Turkish drones, advisers and ammunition: cheap, few Turkish deaths, less visible abroad. They only hold border areas and move slowly.
krieg.einsatz.grund_kueste: No coast within reach: a blockade has no effect here.
krieg.einsatz.grund_stellvertreter: There are no allied forces on the ground here.
krieg.einsatz.grund_abkuehlung: The General Staff is regrouping; possible again in {tage} days.
krieg.einsatz.grund_kapital: Not enough political capital to switch.
krieg.einsatz.grund_aktiv: This type of operation is already in force.
krieg.einsatz.umgestellt: The General Staff switches: against {land} the operation is now “{art}”. Switching costs time and morale.
krieg.tempo.vorsichtig.name: Cautious
krieg.tempo.vorsichtig.text: The General Staff secures every step: fewer losses and a calmer home front, but the front barely moves.
krieg.tempo.normal.name: Normal
krieg.tempo.normal.text: The General Staff weighs speed against losses itself.
krieg.tempo.hart.name: Hard
krieg.tempo.hart.kurz: faster, costly in lives and ammunition
krieg.tempo.hart.text: Advance at any price: the front moves faster, but losses, ammunition use and war-weariness rise sharply.
krieg.ui.kette: Target regions in order of advance
krieg.ui.lage.vorher: The war aim covers {n} regions; there is no fighting yet. Type of operation and pace can be set now at no cost.
krieg.ui.lage.umkaempft: Fighting for {region}. {gelaende}. Taken: {genommen} of {n} target regions.
krieg.ui.lage.alles: All {n} target regions are under Turkish control.
krieg.ui.reichweite: {region} is beyond the reach of “{art}”: only a ground offensive gets further; otherwise the front barely advances.
krieg.ui.einsatz_gemischt: No type of operation chosen yet: the General Staff mixes all forces. A clear choice makes better use of terrain and inventory.
krieg.ui.quelle: Regions around places from Natural Earth; enemy inventory as an index (100 = 2026), generations are game parameters (RECHERCHE_GLM_4).
krieg.besatzung.summe: {n} regions, together about {bip} % of GDP a year
krieg.besatzung.widerstand_hilfe: Resistance tends towards {ziel}: the form of occupation, terrain and relations with the country decide it. Above 50 attacks loom, above 85 an uprising.
krieg.besatzung.form.pufferzone.name: Buffer zone
krieg.besatzung.form.pufferzone.text: Secured militarily, hardly administered civilly: medium cost, medium resistance; tolerated abroad but not recognised.
krieg.besatzung.form_gesetzt.pufferzone: {region} stays under Turkish control as a buffer zone.
krieg.besatzung.form.verwaltung.name: Civil administration
krieg.besatzung.form.verwaltung.text: Schools, power, water, courts: expensive, but resistance falls; in Syria refugees return.
krieg.besatzung.form_gesetzt.verwaltung: In {region} a Turkish civil administration takes over and begins reconstruction.
krieg.besatzung.form.annexion.name: Annexation
krieg.besatzung.form.annexion.text: The region becomes Turkish: hardliners cheer, international law does not. Europe and the US pull away, sanctions become likely, resistance rises.
krieg.besatzung.zurueck_why: The cost of occupation ends and relations ease; nationalists call it betrayal.
krieg.besatzung.anschlag_why: Resistance {widerstand} of 100: every attack costs approval and morale.
krieg.besatzung.aufstand_text: After months of growing resistance {region} can no longer be held: Turkish forces withdraw and the region is lost.
krieg.legende.umkaempft: Contested region: the front is here
krieg.legende.gegner: Target region held by the enemy
krieg.legende.pfeil: Advance: red own forces, dark the enemy
krieg.preis.gefallene_text: {zahl} soldiers have been killed so far in the war with {land}. The opposition forces a debate in parliament; the funerals run on every channel.
krieg.preis.gefallene_warum: Every coffin returns to a province; the opposition asks about the goal and the end.
krieg.preis.sanktion_eu: The EU answers the attack on {land} with trade sanctions.
krieg.preis.sanktion_usa: Washington imposes sanctions over the attack on {land}.
krieg.preis.sanktion_warum: An attack on an ally is not sat out; the sanction only ends after months of détente.
krieg.k.rahmung.verteidigung.name: Self-defence
krieg.k.rahmung.verteidigung.text: A response to an incident: parliament backs it most readily and the world barely counts it against you, provided the escalation serves as proof.
krieg.k.rahmung.schutz.name: Protection of minorities
krieg.k.rahmung.schutz.text: Framed as humanitarian: sellable at home, disputed abroad.
krieg.k.rahmung.beistand.name: Treaty obligation of assistance
krieg.k.rahmung.beistand.text: An alliance obliges: credible only with a treaty in force as proof.
krieg.k.rahmung.revision.name: Open revisionism
krieg.k.rahmung.revision.text: The unframed attack: the cheapest stage for hardliners at home, the costliest abroad; international law and markets settle accounts harshly.
krieg.k.lage.bekannt: The General Staff's picture of the situation is reliable.
krieg.k.lage.vermutet: The picture is patchy; the enemy's strength is an estimate (±10).
krieg.k.lage.unsicher: The picture is uncertain: the General Staff can only roughly gauge the enemy's strength.
krieg.k.paket.paket_ausgewogen.text: Status quo with security guarantees and mutual withdrawal.
krieg.k.paket.paket_weiss.text: Withdrawal without conditions: the cheapest exit, hard to sell at home if the war dragged on.
krieg.k.demob.grund: Demobilisation runs until {datum}; a new mobilisation is possible only after that (90-day bill).
krieg.k.kapital: Not enough political capital for this.
krieg.k.h.bereitschaft.hinweis: Deterrence +3, a small boost in strength; the enemy reads it as escalation (+4).
krieg.k.h.signal.hinweis: Manoeuvres and sharp words: deterrence +2, the conflict cools slightly (−3).
krieg.k.h.vermittlung.hinweis: Bring in mediators: if it works, escalation −18 and conflict −8; the odds depend on standing ({ansehen}) and trust ({vertrauen}).
krieg.k.h.ziel.beleg: Without a treaty in force with this country, the assistance framing is not credible (standing −3 extra).
krieg.k.h.ziel.hinweis: {text} Sets the price of every later step (parliament {stimmen} votes, standing {ansehen}).
krieg.k.h.deeskalation.hinweis: Conflict −10, escalation −12; nationalists at home read it as weakness (−1). Below the calm threshold the episode ends.
krieg.k.h.rueckzug.hinweis: The episode ends: conflict −15, trust +4, but standing −2 and nationalists −3.
krieg.k.h.mobil_teil.hinweis: Call up reserves: clearly more strength; costs 0.3% of GDP, escalation +8, young people −1.
krieg.k.h.mobil_voll.hinweis: The state switches to a war footing: maximum strength; costs 0.7% of GDP, escalation +14, young people −3, urban secularists −2, the home-front clock carries the load.
krieg.k.h.beschluss: Put the deployment motion to parliament
krieg.k.h.beschluss.hinweis: Vote in {tage} days; about {stimmen} of the 301 votes needed are expected. If it fails, it counts as weakness.
krieg.k.h.erlass.hinweis: Bypasses parliament: immediate decision, double cost, trust and legitimacy suffer (−3 / −2.5).
krieg.k.h.verstaerkung.hinweis: Front push +3 next week; costs 0.25% of GDP. The president orders, the General Staff leads.
krieg.k.h.koalition.hinweis: Türkiye asks for assistance: {n} states are still hesitating and can be moved by the request ({bonus} points added to their calculation). Those who refuse take offence (trust −1.5).
krieg.k.h.koalition.rest: The next request will be credible in {tage} days.
krieg.k.h.koalition.niemand: No one is hesitating any more: the rest have refused for good.
krieg.k.h.waffenruhe.hinweis: The enemy accepts if exhausted or if it considers the front lost; if it refuses, the offer counts as weakness at home (clock −3).
krieg.k.h.mobil_nach.hinweis: Possible even mid-war; expensive and late.
krieg.k.h.paket.hinweis: {text} Chance of acceptance about {aussicht}%. The domestic price is already fixed (a free press raises it).
krieg.k.h.weiter.hinweis: Back to the front: the clock loses 5 points, the home front is unsettled.
krieg.k.x.keinspiel: Without the game loop there is no conflict episode.
krieg.k.x.weg: This conflict episode does not exist (any more).
krieg.k.x.phase: This action does not exist in this phase.
krieg.k.x.nicht: That is not possible right now.
krieg.k.x.bereitschaft: The armed forces move to heightened readiness; {land} takes note.
krieg.k.x.bereitschaft.warum: Deterrence +3; the enemy reads it as escalation.
krieg.k.x.signal: Manoeuvres and sharp words aimed at {land}: the standoff remains, but the tone is set.
krieg.k.x.vermittlung.ok: Mediation with {land} is working: channels open up, escalation eases.
krieg.k.x.vermittlung.nein: Mediation with {land} founders on the other side's preconditions.
krieg.k.x.ziel: The government declares its war aim towards {land}: {rahmung}.
krieg.k.x.ziel.warum: The framing sets the price of every later step (parliament {stimmen} votes).
krieg.k.x.ziel.duenn: The proof is thin; other countries take note.
krieg.k.x.deesk: Ankara softens its tone towards {land}; tension eases.
krieg.k.x.deesk.warum: Nationalists read it as weakness; the urban middle breathes a sigh of relief.
krieg.k.x.rueckzug: The government quietly withdraws its position towards {land}; the episode ends.
krieg.k.x.rueckzug.warum: Face suffers more than the situation: standing −2, nationalists −3.
krieg.k.x.voll.text: Full mobilisation is ordered: reserves, materiel, transport plans; the state switches to a war footing.
krieg.k.x.teil.text: Partial mobilisation is ordered: selected reserves and units go on standby.
krieg.k.x.mobil.warum: {bip, number}% of GDP as an extra burden; demobilisation will cost again later (90-day bill).
krieg.k.x.beschluss: The deployment motion against {land} goes to parliament; the vote is in {tage} days.
krieg.k.x.beschluss.warum: Without a majority, tabling it counts as weakness; deals and mood decide.
krieg.k.x.erlass: By decree, bypassing parliament: the deployment against {land} is decided.
krieg.k.x.erlass.warum: Double cost, trust −3, legitimacy −2.5; parliament does not forget the affront.
krieg.k.x.verstaerkung: Reserves and supplies are sent to the front; the General Staff will count them next week.
krieg.k.x.koalition.ja: Ankara asks its partners for assistance: {laender} agree.
krieg.k.x.koalition.nein: The call for assistance goes unanswered: no partner is willing to enter the war.
krieg.k.x.waffenruhe.ja: {land} accepts the ceasefire; the guns fall silent, the negotiating table awaits.
krieg.k.x.waffenruhe.nein: {land} rejects the ceasefire: the other side does not feel exhausted enough.
krieg.k.x.waffenruhe.nein.warum: At home the offer counts as weakness (clock −3).
krieg.k.x.paket.nein: {land} rejects the package (odds {aussicht}%): the other side does not yet feel exhausted enough. The ceasefire holds for now.
krieg.k.x.paket.nein.warum: A rejected package costs nothing but time, yet the clock does not run backwards on either side.
krieg.k.x.weiter: The government orders operations to resume; the home front is unsettled (clock −5).
krieg.k.wr.text1: The guns fall silent in the conflict with {land}. The real bill awaits at the table: border zone, reparations, guarantees, withdrawal.
krieg.k.wr.text2: The domestic price of peace also depends on the press: the freer the media, the more visible and costly every concession.
krieg.k.wr.warum: The ceasefire holds until a peace package or a return to war is decided.
krieg.k.bs.kein: There is no conflict episode against this aggressor; assistance is limited to materiel and diplomacy.
krieg.k.bs.laeuft: A conflict episode with {land} is already under way.
krieg.k.bs.zwei: Türkiye is already handling two conflict episodes; a third cannot be borne.
krieg.k.bs.grund: Victim of the attack, assistance under the pact
krieg.k.bs.notiz: Türkiye joins the case for assistance ({partner})
krieg.k.bs.text1: Türkiye stands by {partner}: the conflict episode with {land} begins at the standoff stage, the framing “assistance” is declared (the pact is the proof).
krieg.k.bs.text2: A deployment decision is still required: parliament or decree, mobilisation and preparation decide how costly the operation will be.
krieg.k.bs.log.warum: Framing “assistance”; the partner stands at Türkiye's side.
krieg.k.bs.ok: Türkiye pledges military assistance to {partner}; the conflict episode with {land} begins.
krieg.k.ang.ok: The ceasefire with {land} takes effect; the negotiating table opens.
krieg.k.beg.angriff: {land} strikes: without a decision of its own, Türkiye is at war; the self-defence framing is obvious.
krieg.k.beg.erlass: By decree the operation against {land} begins; parliament was bypassed.
krieg.k.beg.parlament: With parliament's vote the operation against {land} begins.
krieg.k.beg.front: The front starts at {front} out of 100. The president orders and answers for it; the General Staff leads at the front, and weekly reports show trend and exhaustion.
krieg.k.beg.log.warum: Framing “{rahmung}”; markets react with a risk premium.
krieg.k.bes.ja: Parliament approves the operation against {land} ({ja} to {nein}).
krieg.k.bes.nein: Parliament rejects the deployment motion against {land} ({ja} to {nein}).
krieg.k.bes.nein.warum: The government looks weakened; the other side reads it as an invitation to keep up the standoff.
krieg.k.nl.text.frei: The operation against {land} is lost: reparations, a market risk premium and a disillusioned country. With a free press the loss of approval is as expected ({po, number} points).
krieg.k.nl.text.gelenkt: The operation against {land} is lost: reparations, a market risk premium and a disillusioned country. With a controlled press the loss of approval is as expected ({po, number} points).
krieg.k.nl.offiziere.zerbrochen: In the General Staff, responsibility is discussed openly; the officers' trust is broken.
krieg.k.nl.offiziere.angeknackst: The officers bear the defeat for now; trust is dented, not broken.
krieg.k.nl.chronik: The war ends with reparations and deep domestic damage.
krieg.k.nl.log.warum: Reparations (2% of GDP), markets under pressure, approval −{po, number}.
krieg.k.demob.text1: The reserves come home over {tage} days; the bill keeps running (about {bip, number}% of GDP per month).
krieg.k.demob.text2: A new mobilisation is possible on {datum} at the earliest.
krieg.k.fr.gekauft.notiz: Bought peace: economic ties as collateral
krieg.k.fr.rep_von: Reparations from Türkiye (1.2% of GDP); bought peace creates dependence
krieg.k.fr.preis.frei: The domestic price: approval −{po, number} (with a free press; a free press makes every peace costlier).
krieg.k.fr.preis.gelenkt: The domestic price: approval −{po, number} (with a controlled press; a free press makes every peace costlier).
krieg.k.fr.preiswert: At home the peace stays almost free of cost.
krieg.k.fr.log.warum: Domestic price: approval −{po, number} (press factor {faktor, number}). Markets breathe a sigh of relief (−80 risk points).
krieg.k.fr.maerkte: Markets breathe a sigh of relief (−80 risk points).
krieg.k.kipp.u.text: The situation in the conflict with {land} is worsening: front {front} out of 100, trend falling. Reserves, supply or the road to the negotiating table: room for manoeuvre is shrinking.
krieg.k.kipp.u.warum: The home front reads the casualty reports; the clock falls faster than the front.
krieg.k.kipp.o.text: The situation in the conflict with {land} is clearly improving: front {front} out of 100, trend rising. Success is the best medicine for the home front, and so is the temptation to raise the price of peace.
krieg.k.kipp.o.warum: The General Staff reports territorial gains; the negotiating position grows.
krieg.k.erschoepft.warum: The other side accepts any package that saves face; the table is yours.
krieg.k.droh.log: The situation with {land} escalates into a standoff.
krieg.k.droh.warum: Now every step counts: mobilisation, framing, mediation, or the costly way out.
krieg.k.droh.angriff.warum: The standoff tips into war without a decision of your own; the self-defence framing is obvious.
krieg.k.droh.aus.warum: The tension remains; the episode is not over yet.
krieg.k.demob.fertig.warum: The reserves are discharged; the 90-day bill is paid. A new mobilisation is possible again.
krieg.k.demob.rechnung.warum: Bringing reserves home costs as much as calling them up; until {datum}.
krieg.k.sp.text1: The conflict with {land} has crossed a threshold ({konflikt} out of 100): incidents become an episode that demands decisions of its own.
krieg.k.sp.text2: The escalation phase is the main field of play: readiness, signals, mediation, or declaring a war aim that sets the price of every later step.
krieg.k.sp.log: Tension with {land}: the conflict becomes an episode.
krieg.k.sp.warum: The dossier is in the world view next to the country; every action shows its price there.
krieg.d.schwaecher: clearly weaker than our own forces
krieg.d.staerker: clearly stronger than our own forces
krieg.d.demob: Demobilisation until {datum}: new mobilisation only after that (90-day bill).
